page: Microsoft Azure D8ls_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dlsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573B processor operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2178.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 31.36 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7969.36 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8357.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 620.96 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 66.69 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 283.15 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM, but drops to a weak 7.37 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

The D8ls_v6 does not include local storage, requiring external Premium Storage attachment for persistent data. This design optimizes the instance for stateless workloads or environments where storage is decoupled from compute resources. Qualitatively, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and lack of bundled local storage or public IPv4 addresses make this a cost-efficient option for compute-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the 16 GB memory limit represents a clear tradeoff, rendering the instance unsuitable for large-scale in-memory databases or heavy LLM inference.

This server is best suited for compute-bound workloads such as web serving, where it demonstrates a static web serving throughput of 14.84 GB/sec. It is also well-suited for software compilation, as evidenced by a Geekbench clang compilation score of 9736.0, as well as lightweight serialization, deserialization, and small-scale machine learning inference.
description: The Microsoft Azure D8ls_v6 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an 8-vCPU Intel Xeon 8573B processor running at 4.2 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU) and lacks local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks show strong single-core performance, with Geekbench single-core scoring 2178.0 and gzip compression reaching 31.36 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics remain in the average tier, and text generation for medium 7B LLMs is weak at 7.37 tokens/sec. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, low-memory tasks, making it highly suitable for web serving, software compilation, and lightweight vector processing workloads.
